subject.title: fix(cron): pin the cron webhook bearer token to operator-allowlisted hosts

question: Should existing installations with `cron.webhookToken` and job-record webhook destinations fail closed immediately after upgrade, or should legacy bearer attachment remain until an operator explicitly enables host pinning?
rationale: The PR correctly makes the tradeoff visible, but choosing between credential confinement and uninterrupted authentication for existing persisted destinations changes OpenClaw’s security and upgrade contract and cannot be safely selected by a contributor or automation.

options.title: Approve fail-closed rollout
options.body: Merge the current policy: job-record destinations receive no bearer token until the operator explicitly lists trusted hosts, with Doctor and runtime warnings guiding recovery.

options.title: Preserve legacy authentication by default
options.body: Keep bearer attachment for existing empty-allowlist configurations and introduce host pinning only through an explicitly approved strict mode or staged migration.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed rollout
recommendation.body: Merge the current policy: job-record destinations receive no bearer token until the operator explicitly lists trusted hosts, with Doctor and runtime warnings guiding recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice defines the public security and upgrade policy for a core Gateway credential path.
